claims.claim_text: The indexed Corporal Thomas J. Blakely is confirmed against the exact-name, exact-private-identifier Army record.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official Army merged file contains an exact full-name and private-identifier match for Thomas J. Blakely.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The full name, middle initial, and exact private identifier confirm identity.
claims.temporal_assessment: The electronic Army record is dated October 26, 1946, after OSS dissolution, so it cannot establish pre-OSS employment or occupation.
claims.match_notes: The identifier is withheld publicly. No postwar occupation code is repurposed as pre-OSS evidence.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Corporal Thomas P. Blakenship is confirmed as the Thomas P. Blankenship in the official Army record.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official Army merged file matches the private identifier, first name, middle initial, and all other available military details while spelling the surname Blankenship.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact private identifier confirms the match and establishes Blakenship as an indexed spelling variant of Blankenship for this person.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army record documents entry on November 30, 1942; it does not state the later OSS assignment date.
claims.match_notes: Both spellings remain searchable. The private identifier is withheld publicly.

claims.claim_text: At Army entry on November 30, 1942, Thomas P. Blakenship was recorded as a student; the institution is not identified.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NARA's fixed-width Army record carries occupation code 992, which the corrected official code list defines as students.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact private identifier links the Army record's Blankenship spelling to the index's Blakenship spelling.
claims.temporal_assessment: The dated Army-entry record establishes student status at entry but not the school, employer, or later Army-to-OSS sequence.
claims.match_notes: Student status is not employment and is excluded from verified-employer analytics.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Corporal Hershell O. Blakley is confirmed as the Hershel O. Blakley in the official Army record.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official Army merged file matches the private identifier, surname, middle initial, and available military details while spelling the given name Hershel.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact private identifier confirms the match despite the one-letter given-name difference.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army record documents entry on April 20, 1942; it does not state the later OSS assignment date.
claims.match_notes: Both Hershell and Hershel remain searchable. The private identifier is withheld publicly.

claims.claim_text: At Army entry on April 20, 1942, Hershell O. Blakley's recorded civilian occupation group was farm hands on general farms.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NARA's fixed-width Army record carries occupation code 316, which its corrected code list defines as farm hands on general farms.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact private identifier links the Army record's Hershel spelling to the index's Hershell spelling.
claims.temporal_assessment: The dated Army-entry record is strongly bounded pre-service evidence, but it names no farm or employer and gives no OSS start date.
claims.match_notes: No farm, employer, ownership status, or workplace is named. The occupation is excluded from verified-employer analytics.

claims.claim_text: The indexed CAF-5 Emily Blanas is strongly matched to the Miss Emily Blanas discussed for possible office placement in a contemporaneous OSS administrative letter.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Miss Emily Blanas if she comes would have to work in another office.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A March 1944 OSS administrative letter discusses whether Emily Blanas might be brought to the office and where she could work.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the exact uncommon name, female civilian-office context, contemporaneous OSS record, and later index classification as CAF-5. The personnel file must still confirm the hiring chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: The letter predates or accompanies possible OSS placement; it does not establish where she was working immediately beforehand or whether she had already entered OSS elsewhere.
claims.match_notes: The letter is used only for identity resolution. It is not evidence of a pre-OSS employer, and 'another office' is not normalized as an organization.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Captain Frank T. Blanas is confirmed against the exact-name, exact-rank, exact-private-identifier OSS personnel interview.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The contemporaneous OSS interview identifies Captain Frank T. Blanas of Infantry with the same private officer identifier carried by the index.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact full name, captain rank, branch, and private officer identifier confirm identity across two direct official records.
claims.temporal_assessment: The interview sequences active Army duty from June 1942, OSS assignment in October 1943, and arrival in Cairo and Bari in early 1944.
claims.match_notes: The private officer identifier is withheld publicly. Civilian-life information immediately preceding the Blanas section belongs to the prior interviewee and is not attributed to Blanas.

claims.claim_text: Frank T. Blanas's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was active-duty United States Army service as an infantry officer.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Entered on active duty from the Reserve Corps as an officer June 1942. Assigned to OSS October 1943.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The OSS interview explicitly states that Blanas entered active duty from the Reserve Corps in June 1942 and was assigned to OSS in October 1943.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by the exact private officer identifier, full name, captain rank, and branch across the index and interview.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate military pathway from Army active duty into OSS assignment; the source does not identify the intervening Army unit or exact days.
claims.match_notes: This is a military assignment, not a civilian employer. No civilian occupation or employer before Reserve Corps service is established.
